reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - lovastatin significantly reduced cholesterol (-27.25 mg/dL) and LDL (-25.28 mg/dL), confirming HMG-CoA reductase inhibition. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Mixed evidence of downstream pathway effects. Some biomarkers moved in expected directions (e-cadherin decreased in placebo vs increased in treatment, n-cadherin decreased in placebo vs increased in treatment), but others showed minimal changes (Ki-67, p21, HIF1alpha). The mevalonate pathway appears partially engaged but not robustly. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint clearly missed - histopathologic regression failed to occur with both pathologist assessments showing minimal improvement (effect sizes 0.5 vs -0.12 and 0.17 vs 0.04). No p-values reported but effect sizes suggest no meaningful clinical benefit. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Some suggestion of benefit in preventing nevi progression (1 vs 7 patients had increased nevi count), but this was a secondary observation. 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major trial design issues - adequate duration (24 weeks), placebo-controlled, reasonable sample size (80 patients). This appears to be a case where target engagement occurred but the downstream biology didn't translate to the clinical endpoint.

failure_modes.evidence: Target engagement confirmed by cholesterol/LDL reduction, some biomarker movement suggesting partial pathway modulation, but primary histopathologic regression endpoint failed to improve meaningfully
